items.heading: The Act Uses the Term
items.text: The Act uses the term specific learning disability. A commonly quoted definition calls it a group of conditions with a deficit in processing language, spoken or written, that can show as difficulty in reading, writing, spelling or maths, and includes dyslexia, dysgraphia, dyscalculia, dyspraxia and developmental aphasia.

items.heading: Without a Certificate, Accommodation Depends
items.text: Without a certificate, accommodation depends on goodwill. With one, it is a right to ask. The process has four steps.

items.heading: The Same Student Can Get
items.text: The same student can get three different answers from three bodies. Here is what the documents we read say. Use it to ask the right question, then read the bulletin of the exact exam.

visuals.heading: Exam Help: Who Gives What

rows: The circular of 24 January 2017 lists dyslexic candidates among those who can use a scribe, extra time or both, and who can take one compulsory language instead of two in Class X. A later CBSE manual (December 2024) lists extra time, a scribe or reader, a computer or laptop without internet and basic calculators for eligible students, and asks you to upload a supporting disability document (PDF, up to 2 MB) on the portal.
The two documents differ on calculators, so ask your school which rule applies in your exam year. The Pending option on the portal can be chosen only once.

The CLAT 2024 notification gave candidates with a benchmark disability 40 extra minutes on the two-hour paper, for 2 hours 40 minutes in all. A scribe is allowed for blindness, locomotor disability affecting both arms and cerebral palsy, and for others with a certified limitation that impedes writing. A scribe cannot be linked to a coaching centre.
Check the current year's disability notification. The Consortium also arranges a scribe if you cannot find one and tell it in time.

The ICSI FAQ lists dyslexia, dysgraphia and dyscalculia as special cases. The concessions named are leniency on spelling mistakes, a cover-page stamp and instructions to the examiner. The FAQ does not explicitly grant a scribe or extra time for these, though it gives 20 extra minutes per hour to listed physical and sensory disabilities. Apply in writing at least 45 days before the exam.
The FAQ shows no date, so confirm with ICSI before you plan around it. Other professional bodies set their own rules.
